## Task and approach

We worked with eight classes in VisDrone: person, bicycle, car, van, truck, tricycle, bus and motor. We process frames separately, without using the previous frame. The main problem is how small everything gets after resizing. About half the boxes are under 32 px, and the most crowded clip has around 140 objects per frame.

We compared Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, YOLO11 and RT-DETR, giving each 12 epochs. For submission we kept full-frame YOLO and the YOLO + Faster R-CNN ensemble.

## Data

The size plot was the most useful part of EDA for choosing settings. After resizing to short side 800, with the long side capped at 1333, the median box side is 31.7 px. In total, 50.9% are below 32 px. Default RetinaNet anchors start at 32 px, which seemed large here. We included 16 px anchors and a larger YOLO input in the comparison.

There are far more cars than bicycles, tricycles or buses. People and motors are often just small patches in the frame. We still need to look at the rare classes: mAP weights them equally, even though they account for fewer boxes.

We keep every 10th training frame and every 5th validation frame to cut down on repeated images and training time. The split is by video. Nearby frames are too similar to put on opposite sides of a random split.

Ignored regions needed a separate step. We remove their boxes from the training targets and paint the area with RGB `(123, 117, 104)`, so objects inside it do not become background examples. For validation we use the untouched images and pass `iscrowd` to the evaluator.

YOLO labels use normalised centre coordinates, width and height. Torchvision uses box corners, reserves class 0 for background, and handles resize and normalisation internally after receiving RGB tensors in `[0, 1]`. We added horizontal flips with probability 0.5 there. For Ultralytics we kept the default augmentations, with mosaic off for the last two epochs.

![Ground truth on validation frames: green boxes are objects, red areas are ignored regions](images/gt_overlay_val.png)

## Validation

For the main table we use the same `coco_eval` and original validation frames for every model. It reports mAP at IoU 0.50–0.95, AP50, AP75 and AP by size, with up to 500 detections per image.

The notebook also has three-fold `GroupKFold` for YOLO, grouped by video.

## Models

Every run starts from COCO-pretrained weights, 12 epochs, seed 42.

Faster R-CNN ResNet-50 FPN v2. This was our two-stage baseline. We used SGD, momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0001 and a 300-iteration warmup. The learning rate drops 10× after epochs 8 and 11. The RPN proposes boxes and the second head refines them; for this dataset, the question was whether enough candidates survive in crowded frames.

`frcnn_rpn` doubles the proposals to 4000 train / 2000 test, from 2000 / 1000. Its gain in the table is small. For `frcnn_loss` we changed Smooth L1 to `beta=0.05` and added label smoothing 0.1 together. That is one combined setting, so we cannot say which change helped or hurt.

RetinaNet ResNet-50 FPN v2. We kept the same backbone family for the one-stage anchor-based comparison. There is no proposal stage here, and many anchors only see background. We left focal loss in place and focused on anchor sizes first.

Anchors starting at 16 px fit the size distribution better. With sizes 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, AP_small in the table goes from 0.101 to 0.121. The other setting, focal `alpha=0.35` and `gamma=1.5`. RetinaNet is still behind Faster R-CNN.

YOLO11s / YOLO11m. Resolution matters most in this comparison: 1280 gives a larger gain than changing loss weights to `box=10`, `cls=0.7`, `dfl=2`. YOLO needs no anchor sizes, but tiny objects still have few locations that can be assigned to them. Its assigner uses both class score and box overlap. We used 11s for the baseline experiments and 11m for the larger final setup.

RT-DETR-L. We kept input size 640. The two alternatives were AdamW at lr `2e-4`, and loss weights `bbox=2`, `giou=5`. The latter changes both weights at once; we did not separate their effects. Hungarian matching gives each labelled object one query during training, so this pipeline has no NMS step. The baseline mAP is 0.2200, close to the Faster R-CNN baseline at 0.2197 and below YOLO/1280 at 0.2259. The RT-DETR loss-weight variant reaches 0.2270, above its baseline and YOLO/1280 in this table.

| Run | What we changed |
| --- | --- |
| `frcnn_base` | Faster R-CNN, default RPN |
| `frcnn_rpn` | 4000 / 2000 proposals |
| `frcnn_loss` | Smooth L1 beta 0.05, label smoothing 0.1 |
| `retina_base` | RetinaNet defaults |
| `retina_anchors` | anchors from 16 px |
| `retina_focal` | focal α=0.35, γ=1.5 |
| `yolo_base` | YOLO11s, 960 |
| `yolo_1280` | input 1280 (batch 8 instead of 16) |
| `yolo_box` | box=10, cls=0.7, dfl=2 |
| `rtdetr_base` | RT-DETR-L, 640 |
| `rtdetr_lr` | AdamW, lr=2e-4 |
| `rtdetr_loss` | more GIoU, less L1 |
| `final_yolo` | YOLO11m/1280 on the A40; YOLO11s/960 if VRAM is tight |
| `+full` / `+tiles_nms` / `+tiles_soft` | full frame vs 60% crops |
| `ensemble_yolo_frcnn` | WBF of tiled Soft-NMS YOLO and Faster R-CNN (weights 2:1, IoU 0.55) |

The graph uses the epoch values listed below. RT-DETR has higher mAP from epochs 2 through 11 and peaks at 0.2200 in epoch 11, before falling to 0.2168 in epoch 12. Faster R-CNN reaches its best mAP, 0.2197, in epoch 12. Their best epoch scores are nearly equal; at the final epoch, Faster R-CNN is ahead. The main results table reports these best epoch values for the two baselines. Faster R-CNN also has higher baseline AP50 (0.4421 versus 0.423) and AP_small (0.126 versus 0.115). The input sizes differ (short side 800 with a 1333 cap for Faster R-CNN, 640 for RT-DETR), so these results do not isolate the effect of architecture or establish equal compute budgets.

Tiling was worse than the full frame: minus 0.017 public / 0.011 private with NMS, and 0.013 / 0.008 with Soft-NMS. Resizing a 60% crop to 1280 changes the object scale quite a lot. Cut-off boxes at crop edges are another possible issue, especially when Soft-NMS keeps them at lower scores under the 500-box cap.
The ensemble did better even though it uses the weaker tiled YOLO file: `tiles_soft` at 0.2429 public, mixed with Faster R-CNN at 0.1981. We used WBF with weights 2:1 and IoU 0.55. The result is 0.004 public and 0.009 private above full-frame YOLO.

We selected `final_yolo.csv` and `ensemble_yolo_frcnn.csv`. Those were also the two best private scores.


## Failures

The three examples below show possible failure mechanisms. Green boxes show the labels; orange boxes show the predictions used in each example.

1. The person is missed at threshold 0.30. The original box is only 30 x 20 px; it looks larger here because the crop is enlarged. Resizing could remove enough detail to cause this. Comparing recall on the same frames at 960 and 1280 would help check that.

<img alt="failure case 1" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto" />

Source crop: `val/images/uav0000305_00000_v/0000001.jpg`.

2. The box is in the right place, but the van gets labelled car with score 0.62. From above their shapes can be similar. We would first check how often this particular confusion occurs.

<img alt="failure case 2" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto" />

Source crop: `val/images/uav0000182_00000_v/0000001.jpg`.

3. One box, score 0.73, covers two cars. The model would need two separate boxes here. Crowding could make their features hard to separate, and Soft-NMS cannot fix a box that already contains both cars. Higher input resolution is one thing to test; changing the merge threshold alone will not split it.

<img alt="failure case 3" src="data:image/png;base64," style="max-width:100%;height:auto" />

Source crop: `val/images/uav0000137_00458_v/0000001.jpg`.

## Reproduction

Dependencies are in `requirements.txt`. Training was on a Runpod NVIDIA A40, image `runpod/pytorch:1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404`, PyTorch 2.8.0, CUDA 12.8, Ultralytics 8.4.208.

1. Put `train/`, `val/`, `test/` and `test_images.csv` in the data directory. Set `HW2_DATA` for a local run.
2. Open `notebooks/hw2_detection.ipynb`, set `HW2_PART=all`, run the cells in order. Or run `yolo`, `rcnn` and `detr` on separate GPUs, then `merge`. If the kernel dies on CPU, set `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8` and `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=8`. `HW2_BIG_GPU=0/1` picks batch size; `HW2_WORKERS` sets dataloader workers.
3. Ensemble: `python notebooks/ensemble.py` from the directory that has `out/`, `val/` and `test_images.csv`.
4. Outputs: `out/results_*.csv`, checkpoints in `out/runs/`, submissions in `out/submissions/`.
5. Seed 42 is not enough to match bit-for-bit across GPUs.

If `val_preds_tiles_soft.json` exists, `ensemble.py` scores the same YOLO variant as the test file. Otherwise it scores full-frame YOLO and writes `out/results_ensemble.csv`. Use `check_submission.py` before upload. `python -m pytest tests` covers box conversion, WBF and error bins on CPU.
